source.version: arXiv preprint 2607.26899, downloaded from arxiv.org/pdf/2607.26899; the document shows no arXiv version number or date. Title page: 'This is a preprint of a manuscript that has not undergone peer review.' Writers recruited March 11-15, 2026; evaluators April 13, 2026 (p. 16).
source.title_on_document: Human diversity fuels collective creativity that large language models cannot simulate or sustain

supplement.where: SI Appendix, pp. 23-29 of this PDF. Data, materials, and code at https://osf.io/amgx9/overview?view_only=46c491afd0ba40fc91f361aa2b53be79 (p. 17). Preregistration at https://tinyurl.com/DiverseCreativity (p. 4, p. 20).
supplement.holds: Tables S1-S3 (mixed-model coefficients with 95% CIs and p-values for diversity and ratings), Fig. S1 (metaphor + explanation diversity), Fig. S4 (quantile regressions), Fig. S9 (other preregistered diversity measures), Fig. S10 (LLM-judge scores), prompts Figs. S2, S5-S8. No arm-level SDs or per-arm participant counts anywhere in the PDF.

paper_design_summary: 644 Prolific writers (318 native English, 326 non-native English) each wrote four creative metaphors in a 2 x 3 between-subjects design that crosses writer background with three GenAI conditions: human-only, AI ideation (GPT-4o supplies five candidate metaphors with explanations), and AI refinement (writer writes the metaphor, GPT-4o supplies five candidate explanations). Collective diversity was scored as each metaphor's cosine similarity to the leave-one-out centroid of its condition-by-scenario pool (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), and 351 blind evaluators rated novelty, surprise, aptness, and explanation quality. A non-preregistered extension compares the human pools with pools written by LLM personas built from the writers' backgrounds.

studies.label: Human metaphor-writing experiment (L1/L2 x no AI / AI ideation / AI refinement)

assignment.what_was_assigned: GenAI condition (human-only, AI ideation, AI refinement). Writer background (L1 vs L2) is a measured trait, not assigned. Within the two AI conditions, L2 writers chose their language of AI interaction (self-selected).
assignment.quote: The writing task followed a 2 × 3 between-subjects design, crossing writer background (L1 vs. L2) with GenAI usage (human-only vs. AI ideation vs. AI refinement).
assignment.locator: p. 17, Materials and Methods, Writing task and materials; also p. 4-5 (design overview) and Fig. 1, p. 5
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 4 (link https://tinyurl.com/DiverseCreativity); p. 20, Preregistration and deviations

arms.name: Human-only (No AI)
arms.description: Writers produced metaphors on their own, in English, no GenAI allowed; tab-switch detection ended sessions on a second switch.

arms.name: AI ideation
arms.description: Before each metaphor, GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06) supplied five candidate metaphors with short explanations; writers could adopt, adapt, ignore, or regenerate. L2 writers could interact in their native language and received English translations.

arms.name: AI refinement
arms.description: Writers first wrote their own metaphor, then GPT-4o supplied five candidate explanations for it; the metaphor itself stayed the writer's own. L2 writers could interact in their native language.

participants.exclusions: Sessions terminated for tab or window switching: 24 in human-only, 23 in AI ideation, 18 in AI refinement (pp. 17-18). The paper does not say whether these are inside or outside the 644. The diversity and rating models list N writer = 644 (Tab. S1, Tab. S2, pp. 28-29). Tab. S1 has 2,493 metaphor observations, fewer than four per writer for 644 writers; the gap is not explained. Per-arm counts are not reported; the only arm-related count is 228 L2 writers in the two AI conditions (p. 8, p. 18). Tab. S3 models restricted to the AI conditions use N writer = 441 (ratings) and 440 (centroid similarity).
participants.who: Prolific writers: 318 native English (L1; English sole native language, born and residing in a majority-English-speaking country) and 326 non-native English (L2; 34 native languages, most commonly Arabic, Portuguese, Italian, Polish, Spanish). Mean age 36.1 (SD 12.6), 49% women. Separate panel of 351 native-English Prolific evaluators rated the metaphors.
participants.country: not_stated (L1 writers from majority-English-speaking countries; L2 country not stated)
participants.quote: We preregistered a target of 600 writers, 100 per cell in the 2 × 3 design, and ultimately recruited 644 writers via Prolific between March 11 and 15, 2026.
participants.locator: p. 16, Materials and Methods, Participants (Writers); N writer = 644 in Tab. S1 (p. 28) and Tab. S2 (pp. 28-29)

ai_tool.how_used: AI ideation arm: chat that supplies five candidate metaphor + explanation pairs per scenario, with regeneration on request (ideas_supplied). AI refinement arm: chat that refuses to suggest the metaphor and supplies five candidate explanations for the writer's own metaphor (closest code: refinement). L2 writers in both AI arms chose English or their native language; 84 of 228 chose native language and received English translations to edit (p. 18). System prompts in SI Figs. S5-S8.

task.description: Four scenarios (boring class, disgusting food or drink, worst movie or TV show, messiest room), randomized order; one creative metaphor per scenario in the format 'It feels like ___. This is because ___.' Instructions stressed novel, surprising comparisons.
task.duration: Median completion time 20 minutes for the whole session (p. 16).

outcomes.name: Collective diversity: centroid similarity of metaphor embeddings (metaphor text only)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity of each metaphor ('It feels like ___' text only) to the leave-one-out centroid of all other metaphors for the same scenario in the same condition; higher = less diverse. Sign: 'direction' below refers to diversity, so higher similarity = treatment_lower. Linear mixed model, random intercepts for writer and scenario, treatment-coded so the main condition coefficients are simple effects for L1 writers (p. 19). Chosen as primary among preregistered diversity measures after registration (p. 20).

contrasts.reported: AI ideation (vs No-AI) b = 0.036, 95% CI 0.017 – 0.056, p < 0.001 (simple effect at L1); AI ideation × L2 b = 0.015, 95% CI -0.013 – 0.043, p = 0.284. Means: L1 0.421 (No AI) vs 0.457 (ideation); L2 0.398 vs 0.451. N writer 644, observations 2493. Text p. 7 reports b = 0.036 as 'vs. human-only' without the L1 qualifier.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Tab. S1 (Metaphor column); p. 7 and p. 8 text; Fig. 2A, p. 7

contrasts.reported: AI refinement (vs No-AI) b = 0.007, 95% CI -0.013 – 0.027, p = 0.516 (simple effect at L1); AI refinement × L2 b = 0.005, 95% CI -0.024 – 0.034, p = 0.730. Means: L1 0.421 vs 0.426; L2 0.398 vs 0.409.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Tab. S1 (Metaphor column); pp. 7-8 text; Fig. 2A, p. 7

contrasts.reported: AI refinement (vs ideation) b = -0.037 on centroid similarity, 95% CI -0.052 – -0.023, p < 0.001, additive model on AI conditions only with L2-EN and L2-Non-EN indicators, N writer 440, observations 1707.

diversity_detail.metric: Mean cosine similarity to leave-one-out centroid (higher = more homogeneous)
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each metaphor against the centroid of all other metaphors for the same scenario in the same condition (leave-one-out). Pools are defined by condition and scenario, not by writer background (p. 7 Fig. 2 caption, pp. 18-19).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Linear mixed-effects model on metaphor-level centroid similarity with random intercepts for writer and scenario (statsmodels); 95% CIs and p-values in Tab. S1. Figure error bars are ± SEM.
diversity_detail.notes: L1 vs L2 gaps within condition are reported with p-values (No AI Δ = 0.024, p = 0.003; ideation Δ = 0.006, p = 0.481; refinement Δ = 0.018, p = 0.032; p. 7-8), but writer background is not assigned.

outcomes.name: Collective diversity: centroid similarity of metaphor + explanation embeddings
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Same leave-one-out centroid similarity, but each metaphor embedded together with its explanation (secondary measure, p. 18). Higher = less diverse; direction refers to diversity.

contrasts.reported: AI ideation (vs No-AI) b = 0.028, 95% CI 0.005 – 0.051, p = 0.019 (L1 simple effect); AI ideation × L2 b = 0.027, 95% CI -0.006 – 0.059, p = 0.107.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Tab. S1 (Metaphor + reason column); p. 8 text; Fig. S1, p. 23

contrasts.reported: AI refinement (vs No-AI) b = 0.046, 95% CI 0.022 – 0.069, p < 0.001 (L1 simple effect); AI refinement × L2 b = 0.013, 95% CI -0.021 – 0.046, p = 0.456.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Tab. S1 (Metaphor + reason column); p. 8 text; Fig. S1, p. 23

contrasts.reported: 'the two AI conditions did not differ (b = 0.018, p = 0.12)'

diversity_detail.metric: Mean cosine similarity to leave-one-out centroid (higher = more homogeneous)
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each metaphor + explanation against the centroid of all other entries for the same scenario in the same condition (leave-one-out).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Linear mixed-effects model, random intercepts for writer and scenario; 95% CIs in Tab. S1.

outcomes.name: Collective diversity: mean pairwise cosine distance
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Preregistered alternative collective-diversity measure, reported only in Fig. S9A (higher = more diverse). Embedding model and pairing not described beyond the axis label.

contrasts.reported: Figure only. Caption: 'The primary result is unchanged: AI ideation reduces collective diversity for both groups and narrows the L1–L2 gap, whereas AI refinement preserves it.'
Figure only; caption says AI refinement preserves collective diversity. No test reported.

diversity_detail.computed_over: not stated (pairwise within condition presumably; the paper does not describe it)
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Error bars on figure only; no test reported
diversity_detail.notes: Fig. S9B (semantic distance to prompt) and S9C (lexical diversity, TTR) are recorded as S1-O4 and S1-O5.

outcomes.name: Semantic distance to prompt
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: The paper lists 'semantic distance' among its preregistered collective-diversity measures (p. 20); Fig. S9B plots semantic distance of each output to the prompt, which is a per-output distance, not a comparison across people, so coded here as novelty. Figure only.

outcomes.name: Lexical diversity (type-token ratio)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Preregistered 'lexical diversity' measure; Fig. S9C plots TTR by condition. Paper: 'lexical diversity (C) is near the ceiling and uninformative for these short metaphors.' Coded 'other' because TTR is a property of a single output, not a comparison across people.

contrasts.reported: Figure only; values near ceiling (about 0.98); no test reported.

outcomes.name: Divergent creativity rating (novelty + surprise)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 351 native-English Prolific evaluators, blind to condition and background, rated each metaphor with its explanation on 0-100 sliders; novelty and surprise averaged (Spearman-Brown r = 0.86). Each evaluator rated 24 metaphors. Mixed model with random intercepts for evaluator, writer, scenario; treatment-coded, so condition coefficients are L1 simple effects. Part of the preregistered individual outcome family; human ratings chosen over LLM scoring after registration (p. 20). Quantile regressions in Fig. S4.

contrasts.reported: AI ideation (vs No-AI) b = 4.75, 95% CI 2.00 – 7.50, p < 0.001 (L1); AI ideation × L2 b = -3.92, 95% CI -7.79 – -0.05, p = 0.047. Text: L2 simple effect b = 0.834, p = 0.548. Intercept 53.41. N evaluator 351, N writer 644, observations 8241.
contrasts.locator: pp. 28-29, Tab. S2 (Divergent column); p. 12 text; Fig. 4A, p. 11

contrasts.reported: AI refinement (vs No-AI) b = 2.93, 95% CI 0.15 – 5.71, p = 0.039 (L1); AI refinement × L2 b = -3.14, 95% CI -7.13 – 0.86, p = 0.124. Text p. 12 reports L2 'unchanged (divergent: b = -3.138, p = 0.124)', which equals the interaction term, not an L2 simple effect.
contrasts.locator: pp. 28-29, Tab. S2 (Divergent column); p. 12 text; Fig. 4A, p. 11

contrasts.reported: AI refinement (vs ideation) b = -1.31, 95% CI -3.21 – 0.60, p = 0.178; additive model on AI conditions, N writer 441, observations 5638.

outcomes.name: Convergent creativity rating (aptness/appropriateness + explanation quality)

outcomes.measure_detail: Same 351 blind evaluators; appropriateness and explanation quality averaged (Spearman-Brown r = 0.87). Same mixed model as S1-O6. Note that explanation quality is scored partly on AI-suggested explanation text in both AI arms.

contrasts.reported: AI ideation (vs No-AI) b = 3.13, 95% CI 0.86 – 5.39, p = 0.007 (L1); AI ideation × L2 b = 0.58, 95% CI -2.61 – 3.78, p = 0.720. Text: L2 simple effect b = 3.711, p = 0.001. Intercept 63.65.
contrasts.locator: pp. 28-29, Tab. S2 (Convergent column); p. 12 text; Fig. 4B, p. 11

contrasts.reported: AI refinement (vs No-AI) b = 3.24, 95% CI 0.95 – 5.53, p = 0.006 (L1); AI refinement × L2 b = -1.76, 95% CI -5.05 – 1.54, p = 0.296. Text: L2 'convergent advantage was no longer significant (b = 1.485, p = 0.219)'.
contrasts.locator: pp. 28-29, Tab. S2 (Convergent column); p. 12 text; Fig. 4B, p. 11

outcomes.name: LLM-judge creativity score (Bradley-Terry, standardized within judge)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Preregistered automated LLM-based scoring that the authors set aside after validation. Three judges (GPT-4o mini, Claude Sonnet 4, Qwen3-8B) ranked randomly sampled metaphors; scores z-scored within rater; human panel shown for comparison. Spearman with human panel 0.30-0.37 (figure) / 0.31-0.38 (caption).

contrasts.reported: Figure only: 'two of the three LLM judges (GPT-4o mini, Qwen3-8B) sharply over-reward AI-ideation metaphors and penalize AI-refinement'.

studies.label: LLM persona simulation of the writer pool (not preregistered)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people assigned. For every writer in S1, a persona prompt built from the writer's background was given to GPT-4o mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Qwen3.5-27b, which wrote the same four metaphors; simulated pools compared with human pools.
assignment.quote: For every writer in all three conditions, we constructed a persona prompt from their background questionnaire
assignment.locator: p. 19, LLM simulation of the writer pool; p. 9 text
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 19 and p. 20 ('The LLM simulations ... were not preregistered')

arms.name: Human pools (No AI, AI ideation, AI refinement)
Simulated pools (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Qwen3.5-27b, GPT-4o mini)
arms.description: Persona-conditioned LLM metaphors at default temperature 1.0; extensions with native-language prompting for L2 personas and temperature sweeps 0.5-2.0.

participants.who: No new participants; human comparison pools are the S1 writers, and personas are built from their background data.

ai_tool.how_used: Models write the metaphors themselves from persona prompts; no human receives AI help in this comparison.

task.description: Same four metaphor scenarios and two-part format as S1.

outcomes.name: Collective diversity of simulated vs human pools (centroid similarity)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same leave-one-out centroid similarity as S1-O1. Also checked gibberish share (wordfreq), format adherence, and GPT-2 perplexity.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Simulated pools (each model, default temperature, English output)
contrasts.reported: each simulation vs. human with AI ideation: Claude Δ = 0.102, Qwen Δ = 0.111, GPT-4o mini Δ = 0.241, all p < 0.001 (higher similarity = less diverse). Claude Sonnet 4.6 'recovered only 75.3% of the diversity of the human-only pool'. Native-language pipeline: Claude Sonnet 4.6 vs human AI ideation M = 0.528 vs. 0.457, Δ = 0.071, p < 0.001; GPT-4o mini native vs English-only M = 0.606 vs. 0.698. Temperature plateau around 0.50, gap of 0.04; GPT-4o mini at 2.0 had 14.3% gibberish words.
contrasts.locator: p. 9 text and Fig. 3A; p. 10 text and Fig. 3B-D; Fig. S3, p. 24

diversity_detail.metric: Mean cosine similarity to leave-one-out centroid
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each metaphor against the centroid of the other metaphors in its pool and scenario
diversity_detail.notes: Context evidence only (AI-generated vs human-generated output).

company_involvement.description: Authors at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development; no company affiliation or funding stated. The authors disclose using Claude (Anthropic) for language editing and code drafting.

eligibility.reason: S1 is a preregistered between-subjects online experiment with a no-AI arm and two GenAI arms, 644 writers analyzed (Tab. S1, S2), and outcomes scored on the metaphors (embedding diversity, blind human ratings). The PDF never says that writers were randomly assigned to GenAI condition; 'random' appears only for scenario order, evaluator presentation order, and random intercepts. Writer background is measured, and L2 language of AI interaction is self-selected. If the preregistration or OSF materials confirm random assignment to condition, S1 is core. S2 (LLM personas vs human pools) is ai_vs_human context.

one_line_finding: Relative to no AI, AI ideation raised metaphors' centroid similarity (less collective diversity; b = 0.036, 95% CI 0.017 to 0.056, L1 simple effect) while AI refinement did not (b = 0.007, p = 0.516), and AI ideation raised blind divergent ratings for L1 writers (b = 4.75, 95% CI 2.00 to 7.50) (Tab. S1 and S2, p. 28).
open_questions: Random assignment to GenAI condition is not stated anywhere in the PDF; check the preregistration (tinyurl.com/DiverseCreativity) or OSF materials.

Per-arm participant counts are not reported. Whether the 65 sessions terminated for tab switching (24/23/18) are inside or outside the 644 analyzed is not stated. Tab. S1 has 2,493 metaphors, fewer than four per writer; the gap is not explained.

Fig. S8 (L2 refinement prompt, p. 26-27) repeats the ideation instruction 'provide 5 suggestion pairs of the first and second blanks', which contradicts the refinement condition described on pp. 17-18 and in Fig. S7. Either a copy error in the SI or L2 refinement writers also received metaphor suggestions.

The headline condition coefficients (e.g., b = 0.036 for AI ideation on p. 7) are L1 simple effects under treatment coding (p. 19), though the text presents them as overall effects. The p. 12 statement that AI refinement 'left L2 writers' ratings unchanged (divergent: b = -3.138, p = 0.124; convergent: b = -1.756, p = 0.296)' quotes the interaction terms of Tab. S2, not L2 simple effects.

Ratings standard errors use a rating-level mixed model with evaluator, writer, and scenario random intercepts; diversity uses a metaphor-level model with writer and scenario random intercepts. No participant-level SDs are reported.
notes: The markdown gives the ideation model ID as 'gpt-4o-2024-0806'; the PDF (p. 17) reads 'gpt-4o-2024-08-06'. L2 language-choice contrasts (L1 vs L2-EN vs L2-Non-EN, ordered trend b = -0.025, p = 0.015, Tab. S3) compare self-selected groups within the AI arms and are not recorded as AI contrasts. Quantile regressions of ratings (Fig. S4, p. 25; text p. 13) are not preregistered and not listed as separate outcomes. Search-record lead said N and assignment were not stated; N is stated (644 writers), assignment method is not.
